components.purpose: Forget part of the record deliberately: choose a boundary, read what would become unknowable, confirm it, get the receipt.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column, space-y-4, p-6 — the same skeleton as every confirmation page. Server component, no client JS; every state change is a full navigation. Which of the four bodies renders is decided in order: receipt (trimmed param present), choose-boundary (no readable date, with or without a rejected one to report), nothing-to-trim, then describe-confirm. DT-0014 has landed: every message block on this page now wears a house role rather than the anonymous border it was built with — consequence for what would go, danger for a rejected date, notice for the receipt, quiet for nothing-to-trim — so the page no longer states four different kinds of fact in one voice.
constraints: The trim is a describe→confirm→perform ceremony — openspec/specs/signal-recording/spec.md:203-209 ('through the same describe→confirm→perform ceremony as its other destructive acts'). A design must not collapse choosing, confirming, and performing into fewer steps.

The description renders before anything is offered — openspec/specs/signal-recording/spec.md:219-224 ('WHEN an operator chooses a boundary date THEN the page states the runs, captures, failed attempts, coins and date span that would go'). The consequence must stay readable before the button that performs.
Rendering the description deletes nothing however many times it renders — openspec/specs/signal-recording/spec.md:243-245. Choosing a boundary must remain a GET navigation, never a POST.
The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS, no hydration. A design requiring client-side interactivity changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

This page has no `?authority=` branch and needs none: the trim is a local record operation keyed on userId, and `TrimRecordResult` is `trimmed | refused` with no authority-lost arm. The `<AuthorityLost>` page the three agent ceremonies gained in `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal` does not apply here — a design must not invent one for symmetry.

DT-0014's four roles are the page's grammar and all four are implemented: consequence for what would go, danger for a rejected date, notice for the receipt, quiet for nothing-to-trim. A ticket that gives two of them the same treatment reverts the ticket.

components.purpose: Choose the date before which the record is forgotten — a question about the record, not yet an act.

actions.effect: GET ?before=YYYY-MM-DD — navigates to the description of what that boundary would take. Deletes nothing.

components.current_implementation: method=get form, flex flex-wrap items-end gap-3. A LABEL-wrapped native date input wearing CONTROL (required), a BUTTON_PRIMARY submit 'Describe what would go', and a BUTTON_SECONDARY anchor 'Leave the record alone'. In the unreadable-date state a role=alert paragraph above the form quotes the unparsable value and points back at the picker; since DT-0014 it wears danger — rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary — because a rejected input is a bounced attempt, not an advisory. The form and both controls were untouched by that ticket.
constraints: The form must stay method=get — choosing a boundary is a question, and the describe it navigates to is effect-free by spec (openspec/specs/signal-recording/spec.md:243-245). A POST here would present choosing as committing.
Control and label treatments come from the CONTROL and LABEL constants in control.ts, shared product-wide — not a per-page className.
The unreadable-date paragraph keeps role=alert.

The submit label must keep saying what it does and does not do — 'Describe what would go' is a look, not a delete; a label that reads like the destructive act would collapse the ceremony's first step.

components.purpose: Show the refusal that bounced a submitted trim back to the person who clicked it.
components.current_implementation: The shared `CarriedProblem` component (src/presentation/components/carried-problem.tsx). CHANGED since the last survey: the inline `{problem ? … : null}` copy this page held is gone and the component is imported — the two-spellings risk this manifest flagged is closed, and `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` now fails any file that hand-rolls the paragraph again. The treatment is unchanged, DT-0004's danger: rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert, opening with a semibold 'Refused: ' prefix, returning null when there is no problem. Untouched by DT-0014, which left it alone by name. What did NOT change is where it is mounted: the describe-confirm branch only, which is where `performTrim` always bounces to (the redirect carries `before=` back, so the describe re-runs). The other three branches still mount nothing.
constraints: role=alert must survive.

The refusal reason is the platform/domain's wording for why nothing was deleted (openspec/specs/signal-recording/spec.md:226-229, 'nothing is deleted and the refusal says why') and must be shown, not summarized.
This is a failed attempt, not advisory — it takes a stronger role than the nothing-to-trim answer and shares its palette with nothing else on the page.

Shared by eleven pages now (agent deploy/undeploy/rebind/archive/reactivate, strategy archive/restore/fork, both /pending surfaces, recorder trim) — restyle it in the component, never per page. A ticket that restyles the bounced-write banner reaches all eleven at once, which is the point of the extraction.
Rendering nothing when there is no problem is load-bearing — a design must not give it a reserved empty slot or a placeholder.
The 'Refused: ' prefix is part of the treatment — a design may restyle the prefix but must not drop the naming of the state.

components.purpose: State what becomes unknowable, before the button that makes it so.
components.current_implementation: role=alert paragraph, rounded-gc-2 border border-consequence-border bg-consequence-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary — the domain's consequence sentence verbatim. DT-0014 moved it off the anonymous border it was built with onto the house consequence role, the one plan-review and the agent archive page already wore; it is the heaviest fact on the page and now reads as such.
constraints: The text is the describe's verbatim consequence sentence — the spec makes its content binding (openspec/specs/signal-recording/spec.md:207-209: 'The description SHALL state what becomes unknowable: how many runs, captures and failed attempts go, across which coins, spanning which dates, and that nothing trimmed can ever be re-recorded'). A design must not paraphrase, truncate, or collapse it behind a disclosure.
Consequence outranks everything on a screen (system.json principle) — this block must not become lighter than the buttons below it.
role=alert must survive.

components.purpose: Carry the trim decision: one committing button, one visible way out.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with before, describedRuns, confirmationToken; success redirects to the receipt state, refusal redirects back here with ?problem=

components.current_implementation: flex flex-wrap gap-3 form; three hidden inputs carry the confirmation binding (before as ISO instant, describedRuns, confirmationToken). Still a wrapping row with no mobile full-width stack: DT-0016/0017/0018 gave the three agent ceremonies the flex-col…tablet:flex-row treatment and did not reach this page, so the product's confirmation rows are now two shapes rather than one. No pending/loading state between click and redirect — the same gap filed as #153 for the archive page.
constraints: The hidden binding (before, describedRuns, confirmationToken) is the confirmation ceremony — openspec/specs/signal-recording/spec.md:215-217 ('the confirmation SHALL be bound to the boundary and the described extent, so agreement to one trim cannot authorise a different one'). The form must keep exactly one submit path.

A submit without the minted confirmation, or with one minted for a different boundary or extent, deletes nothing (openspec/specs/signal-recording/spec.md:226-229) — a design must not add a second control that could bypass the binding.
Cancel must remain a visible peer of the submit, never a text link beneath it (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).

components.purpose: Commit the trim. Named with the described extent: 'Trim <N> runs permanently'.
components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (44px), rounded-gc-2, hover to accent.hover over duration-fast, active holds hover at duration-instant. The label carries the run count and the word 'permanently', pluralized.
constraints: Deliberately NOT danger-styled — DT-0002's ruling, restated in control.ts: trimming after reading the description is the legitimate action; the weight belongs on the consequence block. A design ticket restyling this as danger contradicts a decided ruling.
The label must keep the described run count and 'permanently' — it is the extent the confirmation is bound to, said back at the moment of commitment.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts, shared by every committing submit in the product — not a per-page className.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: Walk away with the record whole.
components.current_implementation: An anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, hover to border-border-strong + bg-bg-sunken over duration-fast, active holds it at duration-instant. Two wordings on this page: 'Leave the record alone' beside the boundary form, 'Keep the record whole' beside the perform form.
constraints: Must remain an anchor (pure navigation, no form participation) and must remain a visible peer of the submit.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).

components.purpose: Say that the chosen boundary would take nothing, and offer the two sensible next moves.

actions.effect: Anchor back to /recorder/trim to pick a different date

components.current_implementation: h1 'Nothing to trim', the describe's reason as a role=status paragraph, then two underlined text links separated by a middot: 'Choose a different date' and 'Back to the record'. Since DT-0014 the reason wears quiet — rounded-gc-2 border border-quiet-border bg-quiet-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary — rather than being a bare text-sm line: this is the page's absence-of-effect sentence, and the system principle gives absence the same visual commitment as a warning without letting it near danger's palette. The two links deliberately stayed text links rather than becoming targets, which is the precedent DT-0015 then cited for the strategy editor's two-choice rows.
constraints: role=status must survive — this is an answer, not an error.
Both links must stay, and in this order: another attempt first, the way out second.
Quiet, never danger — the boundary took nothing, which is a fact about the record and not a failure of the request.

components.purpose: State what the record holds now, after a trim — read from the record, never from the address.

actions.effect: Anchor to /recorder, which renders the same coverage read

components.current_implementation: h1 'Record trimmed', then a role=status notice paragraph saying the reading is taken as the page renders and is not a copy of what the trim reported, then <RecordCoverage> — the same component /recorder uses, carrying its own three arms (per-series rows with counts and gaps / 'Recording has not started.' / 'The record could not be read.' with the reason and the does-not-mean-empty sentence). Then an underlined 'Back to the record' link. Since DT-0014 the notice paragraph wears rounded-gc-2 border border-notice-border bg-notice-subtle.
constraints: No figure on this page may come from the query string. The ?trimmed= parameter is a marker only — it carries no counts, and rendering one from it would restore the forgeable receipt that `the-receipt-states-what-remains` removed.
The three arms of RecordCoverage may not borrow each other's wording: 'could not be read' must never render as 'nothing is recorded'.
Server-rendered with no client JS; every state change is a full navigation.

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, connect link an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY (DT-0006) at the 44px floor. Used by every authenticated page, so this treatment is inherited everywhere.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Trim the record
steps: pick a boundary date, 'Describe what would go'
read the consequence — runs, captures, failures, what becomes unknowable
back to the record, coverage begins where the trim left it

flows.name: The boundary takes nothing
steps: pick a date before the record begins
choose a different date or go back

flows.name: The trim is refused after submit
steps: confirmation fails to consume (boundary or extent moved)
redirected back to the description with ?problem=
problem banner states the reason above the still-usable form

accessibility.notes: problem, consequence, and the unreadable-date paragraph carry role=alert; the receipt and nothing-to-trim reasons carry role=status. Since DT-0014 those roles are also carried visually — danger, consequence, notice, quiet — so the four kinds of fact are no longer told apart by their ARIA role alone. No client JS: every state change is a full navigation, so each state is reached in normal document order rather than a live region.
